title: Hierarchical trip-point fallback & adaptive circuit-breaker for routing
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Goal: Implement an adaptive, hierarchical fallback trigger and circuit-breaker state machine that reduces unnecessary fallbacks while keeping customer-facing SLOs intact. This ticket defines trip-point semantics, short/long window aggregation (EWMA + percentile), token/burst-aware 429 handling, probation windows for model-variant re-enablement, and operator controls for emergency open/close. The implementation must integrate with routing policies (region selection and tier routing) and support per-customer thresholds where SLAs require it.
rationale: Current fallback behavior is too binary: brief spike in 429s causes immediate fallbacks that increase cost and sometimes lower quality. We need a nuanced mechanism that distinguishes bursts vs sustained failures, factors request token sizes, and provides safe automatic re-enablement. This preserves availability without excessive model switching and reduces oscillation during degraded conditions.
design_decisions: Use a two-tier aggregation: short-window EWMA (1-2m) for fast detection + long-window percentile (10-30m) for stability/hysteresis.
Measure error signal as composite metric: 429_rate, timeout_rate, backend_5xx_weighted_by_latency, and synthetic_probe_failures.
Introduce circuit states: CLOSED, SOFT_OPEN (probation sampling allowed), HARD_OPEN (block routing to variant), and PROBATION (gradual traffic ramp to candidate).
Token-aware 429 handling: treat 429s from long-token requests with higher weight for cost/throughput impact; short bursts from small-token requests are de-emphasized.
Tier-aware policies: tiered thresholds (free, standard, premium) with ability to override per-customer SLA flags.
Grace windows: require sustained trip for T_detect and sustained healthy window for T_recover before state transitions to avoid flapping.
Expose operator overrides via Console feature flag and emergency API (runtime-circuit/:id/open|close).
Integrate with synthetic canary probes that exercise critical model variants in each region every N minutes to surface silent failures.
acceptance_criteria: Routing layer supports EWMA and percentile aggregations for error metrics and exposes them to the decision engine.
Circuit-breaker state transitions implemented with CLOSED, SOFT_OPEN, HARD_OPEN, PROBATION semantics and documented thresholds.

Automatic fallback trigger fires only when composite metric exceeds configured hierarchical thresholds for the configured detection window (tests using synthetic traffic prove no false-positive on bursts).
Probation logic successfully ramps 1% -> 5% -> 20% of traffic to a recovered variant before marking it healthy; rollback on relapse.
Per-tier and per-customer override rules are respected in integration tests (including premium exempted from automatic HARD_OPEN unless operator-approved).
Telemetry: Datadog dashboard shows EWMA, percentile latencies, token-distribution histogram, circuit-state, and probe results; alerts created for SOFT_OPEN->HARD_OPEN transitions.
Operator controls (console + API) can force-open/force-close circuits and add temporary suppression TTLs.
implementation_plan: 1) Add EWMA and percentile aggregators to metrics pipeline (short-window 60s EWMA, long-window 20m p95/p99).
2) Extend routing decision engine to evaluate composite metric and consult hierarchical thresholds stored in service config (JSON schema).
3) Implement state machine with persistence in Redis/etcd and add probation sampling hooks in the router.
4) Token-aware weighting: enrich request envelope with token_estimate metadata for routing decisions.
5) Add synthetic probe daemon in each region and wire probe results into the composite metric.
6) Console/UI: status indicators per-model-variant + operator action buttons and audit log entries.
7) Add automated tests: unit, integration (multi-region simulated load), and chaos tests that introduce 429/timeouts.
testing_plan: Unit tests for EWMA implementation (edge cases, warm-up).
Integration test using load generator: short high-burst small-token traffic should not trigger fallback within 2x baseline, sustained error pattern should.
Chaos test: simulate region outage and verify circuit transitions, probation, and downstream traffic reroute.
Regression test: ensure existing fallback rollbacks work with canary rollout pipeline.
Load test: ensure enriched routing decision path adds <1ms median overhead under 95th-percentile QPS.
monitoring_alerts: Alert: 'circuit_state_change' when any model-variant moves to HARD_OPEN for >30s (severity: P1).
Alert: 'ewma_error_rate' when short-window EWMA > configured short_threshold for >45s (severity: P2).
Alert: 'probation_failures' when probation rollback occurs twice within 1 hour (severity: P1).
Dashboard: composite routing health with annotated circuit events and probe failures.
SLO burn rate alert integration per-customer when automatic fallback is triggered for >5% of requests in 10m.
rollout_plan: Feature flag behind 'adaptive_circuit_v2' with gradual ramp: 0% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% traffic over two weeks.
Start in staging with canary region us-west-2; enable synthetic probes and collect baseline measurements for one week.
Enable for internal customers and non-critical tiers, monitor for false positives, then enable premium with more conservative thresholds.
Post-rollout 48h watch with on-call engineer assigned to routing pager and clear rollback playbook in console.
notes: Trade-off: EWMA allows faster detection but is sensitive to tuning; using two windows mitigates premature decisions.
We avoid global fixed thresholds; instead thresholds are percentiles relative to baseline for each model-variant/region pair to account for heterogeneity.
Operator safety: add 'hard-safety-cap' per-tenant to prevent automatic routing changes that could violate contractual SLAs without explicit approval.
